chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Abu al-Faraj al-Sindi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was circumambulating with him around the House, and he said, 'Which of these is the greatest in sanctity?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, you are more knowledgeable about this than I.' He repeated to me, so I said to him, 'The inner part of the House.' He said, 'The Yemeni Corner is a door from the doors of Paradise, open for the Shiah of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), closed for others, and there is no believer who supplicates at it except that his supplication ascends until it adheres to the Throne, with no veil between it and Allah, the Exalted.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.شِيعَةُ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Shiah/Followers of the Family of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the Yemeni Corner in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the Yemeni Corner (Rukn al-Yamani) as a unique spiritual gateway, explicitly linking its openness to Paradise with the *Shi'ah* of the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby emphasizing the theological concept of *Walaayah* in ritual practice. The description of supplications ascending directly to the Throne without a veil underscores the special intercessory status of the faithful in this tradition, reinforcing the Kaaba not merely as a physical structure but as a locus of divine proximity for the Shiah.
